Cyient is both an active Zerodha holding (92 shares, 2.50% weight) and a fresh-capital candidate. web_blocks.caption: Both Sides of the Aisle: Bull Steelman vs. Bear / Skeptic Steelman (Post-Pass 1 Forensics)
headers: The Bear / Skeptic Case (How It Breaks)
rows: Semiconductors & GlobalFoundries
Nov 18–19 $10M CCPS check from Tier-1 foundry GlobalFoundries ($510M post-money, matching EAAA) validates Cyient Semi's custom ASIC/Kinetic roadmap alongside +240.8% YoY revenue [10][11].

Cyient Semi posted a -₹30 Cr Q2 FY27 EBIT loss on product R&D, faces foundry/memory constraints risking 1–2 quarter FY28 breakeven slippage, has no binding wafer volume, and grants SHA preference/exit rights [10][14].
Real strategic validation, not a blank check. Apply a 35% execution/CCPS discount until Semi EBIT losses narrow.
Balance Sheet & TAO Earnouts
FY26 CFO was ₹787 Cr (118% CFO/EBITDA) and Q2 DET FCF hit ₹214 Cr (~140% PAT conversion), providing organic cash flow to service debt [1][14].

Gross borrowings jumped 6.4x to ₹2,759 Cr (0.54x equity, already above CRISIL's <0.50x expectation) AND Other Liabilities jumped ₹1,590 Cr on ₹926.80 Cr TAO earnouts (~₹3,686 Cr / 0.72x equity total), after ₹71.2 Cr FY26 aborted-M&A and ₹27.8 Cr goodwill charges [4][13][15].
The #1 underwriting risk. Earnout cash claims slow bank-debt retirement; fresh capital cannot ignore 0.72x combined obligations.
Core DET, DLM & Leadership

DET EBIT hit a 10-quarter high of 14.2% (₹237 Cr) with record $158.4M Q2 order intake (+21% YoY); DLM holds a record ₹2,813.7 Cr backlog (1.6x book-to-bill) plus Nov 14 HSL maritime defense MoU [3][14][16][21].

DET organic constant-currency growth was just +0.4% YoY, standalone Q2 took a ₹46.0 Cr FX loss, DLM CCC sits at 119 days, and C-suite churn continued (COO Prabhakar Atla Sep 28; CPO Kavita Kurup Nov 17) [1][4][12][14].
Operational stabilization is credible, but organic growth, DLM cash conversion, and executive stability still require Q3–Q4 proof.
Valuation & Stage 2 Tape
Upgraded to Stage 2 (Markup) on both 23 Nov ledger (₹1,160.50) and 25 Nov live TV (₹1,151.20), +2.27% vs 10W EMA, 8.57% VCP squeeze, 4H turn confirmed [28][34].
At 33.83x TV TTM P/E (above LTTS 28.81x & KPIT 26.46x), CMP R:R is inverted at 0.88:1 vs ₹1,310 Base Target and ₹970.95 stop, on thin 0.24x volume in narrow breadth (55.2% >50D) [28][29][34].
Hold existing 92 shares with ratcheted ₹970.95 stop; refuse fresh capital until ₹1,043–₹1,095 support (1.73:1–3.71:1 R:R) + Q3 deleveraging.
web_blocks.takeaway: Cyient is a confirmed Stage 2 turnaround with real GlobalFoundries validation—yet ~₹3,686 Cr of debt+earnouts, -₹30 Cr Semi burn, +0.4% organic DET growth, and 0.88:1 CMP R:R forbid chasing fresh capital.

Stage 2 VCP squeeze (8.57% BB width, 4H turn confirmed), but 0.24x volume and 0.88:1 CMP R:R make chasing ₹1,151.20 poor risk management. Wait for ₹1,043.00–₹1,095.00 (Pivot S1 / 200D EMA shelf).

Long-Term (3–5 Years)
Conditional Compounder
Aero/rail ER&D + DLM defense EMS + GlobalFoundries-backed ASICs is compelling, but consolidated ROCE (12.3%) must climb above 16–18% and C-suite churn must cease before earning CORE_ALPHA.

book_paragraphs: We have arrived at the synthesis—and this refresh is a masterclass in why we always separate business forensics from market headlines. Over the past two weeks, Cyient handed investors two competing realities at once. On the tape, GlobalFoundries' November 18–19 $10 million CCPS investment at a $510 million post-money valuation lifted Cyient back into a confirmed Stage 2 uptrend with an 8.57% VCP squeeze and a confirmed 4-hour turn. In the footnotes, however, Pass 1 blind-spot forensics uncovered ₹926.80 crore of TAO Digital contingent earnouts pushing combined debt-like obligations to ~₹3,686 crore (0.72x equity, above CRISIL's <0.50x expectation), a -₹30 crore Q2 Semiconductor EBIT loss, just +0.4% DET organic constant-currency growth, ₹71.2 crore of FY26 aborted-M&A charges, and fresh COO and CPO departures.

Let us weigh both sides of the aisle with zero hedging. The Bull case is tangible: Sukamal Banerjee lifted Q2 FY27 DET EBIT margins to a 10-quarter high of 14.2% (₹237 crore EBIT, ₹214 crore FCF, and record $158.4 million order intake), Cyient DLM built a record ₹2,813.7 crore backlog (1.6x book-to-bill) plus a November 14 maritime defense MoU with Hindustan Shipyard, and GlobalFoundries' equity check validates Cyient Semiconductors' custom ASIC platform alongside EAAA's May financing. If those engines fire together, normalized FY28E EPS reaches ₹50–52 (and up to ₹54–55 in our Bull Case).

The Bear case is equally concrete and cannot be brushed aside by a headline rally. Reported borrowings of ₹2,759 crore (0.54x equity) already breach CRISIL's <0.50x medium-term gearing expectation, and adding ₹926.80 crore of TAO Digital contingent earnouts lifts total debt-like commitments to ~₹3,686 crore (0.72x equity)—meaning earnout cash checks will compete directly with bank-debt paydown over FY27–FY28. Meanwhile, Cyient Semiconductors is losing ₹30 crore a quarter in EBIT with foundry and memory bottlenecks threatening its FY28 breakeven, GlobalFoundries disclosed no binding wafer-volume commitment while securing CCPS liquidation preference and exit rights, DET's organic constant-currency growth was barely positive at +0.4% YoY, standalone Q2 took a ₹46.0 crore FX loss, DLM's Cash Conversion Cycle sits at 119 days, and C-suite churn continued with COO Prabhakar Atla (Sep 28) and CPO Kavita Kurup (Nov 17) exiting.

Weighting those outcomes—25% Bear at ₹840.00, 50% Base at ₹1,310.00, and 25% Bull at ₹1,620.00—produces a 12-to-18 month probability-weighted expected value of ₹1,270.00 (+10.3% vs the 25 November live TV close of ₹1,151.20; +9.4% vs the 23 November NSE ledger close of ₹1,160.50). Now check the reward-to-risk ratio against our newly ratcheted structural stop at ₹970.95: at ₹1,151.20, you risk ₹180.25 (-15.66%) to make ₹158.80 (+13.79%)—an inverted 0.88-to-1 ratio (0.79-to-1 at ₹1,160.50). That fails our 1.50-to-1 institutional hurdle by a wide margin.

That math dictates our New Capital Verdict: WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT. We refuse to chase a thin-volume (0.24x) Stage 2 bounce at ₹1,151.20 when Earnout-Adjusted EV sits at 23.0x FY26 FCF and debt-free LTTS trades at a lower trailing P/E (28.81x vs 33.83x). Fresh capital waits patiently for a pullback into the ₹1,043.00–₹1,095.00 structural support zone (anchored on Pivot S1 ₹1,042.93 and the 200-day EMA ₹1,041.93), where reward-to-risk jumps to 1.73-to-1 at the top of the band and 3.71-to-1 at the bottom—paired with Q3 FY27 evidence that gross borrowings are stepping down below ₹2,500 crore and Semi losses are narrowing.

For your existing position, the verified 23 November 2026 Zerodha ledger shows 92 shares at an average cost of ₹1,114.24 (₹1,02,509.70 cost basis), worth ₹1,06,766.00 (+₹4,256.30 / +4.15%, or 2.50% of your ₹42,64,304.99 Indian net worth) on the 23 November ledger and ₹1,05,910.40 (+3.32%) on the 25 November live tape. Because Cyient has reclaimed a confirmed Stage 2 uptrend above its rising 30-week SMA (₹992.74) at a disciplined 2.50% weight, our Holding Action is HOLD_WITH_HARD_STOP (0 shares sold today), while ratcheting our hard exit stop UPWARD from ₹951.20 to ₹970.95. Keep 100% of marginal cash in CASH today, monitoring shortlist compounder Coforge (₹2,060.00, ACCUMULATE_ON_DIP, 1.67:1 support R:R) and outside peer LTTS (₹4,178.00) on pullbacks.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION — Ratcheting the Stop Is How You Respect Both Sides
book_callouts.text: Raising our hard stop from ₹951.20 to ₹970.95 lets our 92 held shares ride the confirmed Stage 2 VCP breakout toward ₹1,310 while cutting our worst-case downside. Simultaneously refusing fresh capital at 0.88:1 R:R keeps us from overpaying for a GlobalFoundries headline before the ₹3,686 crore debt-and-earnout load begins shrinking.

book_subsections.title: Exact Execution Math, Three Non-Emotional Alerts & Cash Redeployment
paragraphs: Let us translate every piece of this refresh into exact, executable rules so emotion never enters the picture. First, why is our New Capital Verdict WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT instead of IMMEDIATE_BUY—even though Cyient is now STAGE_2 / CLEAR_FOR_CONSIDERATION with an 8.57% VCP squeeze and a confirmed 4-hour turn? Because technical trend clearance is a necessary condition, never a sufficient one. At ₹1,151.20 (25 November live TV), risking ₹180.25 down to our ₹970.95 stop to chase ₹158.80 of upside to our ₹1,310.00 Base Case target produces a 0.88:1 reward-to-risk ratio. Buying sub-1:1 asymmetry on a CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL business carrying 0.72x combined debt-and-earnout leverage is how portfolios suffer permanent capital drag.

Now look at what happens when we let price come to our ₹1,043.00–₹1,095.00 structural support band (centered around the 20-day swing low at ₹1,065.80, Pivot S1 at ₹1,042.93, and the 200-day EMA at ₹1,041.93). At ₹1,095.00—the top of the band—your downside to ₹970.95 shrinks to ₹124.05 (-11.33%) while your upside to ₹1,310.00 expands to ₹215.00 (+19.63%), delivering a 1.73:1 reward-to-risk ratio. At the ₹1,069.00 midpoint, R:R jumps to 2.46:1, and at ₹1,043.00 it reaches 3.71:1. That is how we enforce our 1.50:1 minimum hurdle without inflating our fundamental target.

Second, manage your existing 92 Zerodha shares (₹1,02,509.70 cost basis, 2.50% portfolio weight) with three crisp alerts: (1) Hard Stop Exit at ₹970.95 (ratcheted up from ₹951.20) — exit all 92 shares on a daily close below ₹970.95 to protect capital against Stage 2 failure or earnings/debt disappointment; (2) Support Re-Underwrite Trigger at ₹1,095.00 — evaluate adding only if price holds ₹1,043.00–₹1,095.00 AND Q3 FY27 filings confirm gross borrowings falling below ₹2,500 crore with DET EBIT >=14.0%; and (3) Strength Trim Trigger at ₹1,310.00 — trim 46 shares (50% of the position) into our Base Target if combined debt plus TAO earnouts remain elevated or Semiconductor EBIT losses have not narrowed from -₹30 crore per quarter.

Third, our 100%-reconciled redeployment plan for the next marginal ₹1,00,000 cash unit retains 100% in CASH today. Why? Because Indian market breadth has narrowed to 55.2% above the 50-DMA, Cyient's CMP R:R is 0.88:1, and better-quality alternatives are either waiting for their own dip zones—such as shortlist IT/Engineering compounder Coforge (25 Nov live TV CMP ₹2,060.00, ACCUMULATE_ON_DIP inside ₹1,951.99–₹2,036.18, Base Target ₹2,620.00, 1.67:1 support R:R, 23.5% ROCE, 0.27x D/E)—or offer sub-1:1 CMP R:R like outside peer LTTS (₹4,178.00, Base Target ₹4,750.00, 0.85:1 CMP R:R vs ₹3,505.22 stop). Keeping cash ready while your 92 held shares participate in Cyient's Stage 2 uptrend gives you the best of both worlds.

Finally, keep our three Q3–Q4 FY27 upgrade and exit signposts taped to your desk. To upgrade Cyient toward active accumulation, we need: (a) gross borrowings stepping down below ₹2,500 crore toward CRISIL's <0.50x expectation; (b) Semiconductor EBIT burn narrowing meaningfully from -₹30 crore per quarter on track for FY28 breakeven; and (c) DET sustaining >=14.0% EBIT while accelerating organic constant-currency growth above +5% YoY with stable C-suite leadership. Conversely, a daily close below ₹970.95, DET EBIT slipping under 12.5%, or fresh debt-funded M&A before TAO Digital and Kinetic prove their ROIC triggers an immediate exit.

Pause for a moment and appreciate why this two-pass discipline works so well in real markets. Had we looked only at the November 18–19 GlobalFoundries headline and the Stage 2 VCP breakout on TradingView, we might have chased ₹1,151.20 with fresh capital at an inverted 0.88:1 reward-to-risk ratio—blindsided by ₹926.80 crore of TAO Digital contingent earnouts, a -₹30 crore quarterly Semiconductor EBIT loss, and ongoing COO/CPO turnover. Conversely, had we looked only at those Pass 1 footnotes, we might have dumped all 92 Zerodha shares at a 2.50% weight right as the weekly tape reclaimed Stage 2 above a rising 30-week average. By holding our existing shares under a tighter, ratcheted ₹970.95 hard stop while demanding the ₹1,043.00–₹1,095.00 support shelf (1.73:1–3.71:1 R:R) and Q3 deleveraging proof for any fresh rupee, we let evidence and asymmetry—never FOMO or fear—run the portfolio.
